heading.en: Every crate fetches the same price

hook.en: If each crate sells for ₹12, the 10th crate brings in exactly as much as the 1st. That simple fact shapes all the *revenue* curves of a competitive firm.
hook.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ಕ್ರೇಟ್ ₹12ಕ್ಕೆ ಮಾರಾಟವಾದರೆ, 10ನೇ ಕ್ರೇಟ್ ಮೊದಲನೆಯದಷ್ಟೇ ಆದಾಯ ತರುತ್ತದೆ. ಈ ಸರಳ ಸತ್ಯವೇ ಸ್ಪರ್ಧಾತ್ಮಕ ಸಂಸ್ಥೆಯ ಆದಾಯ ವಕ್ರರೇಖೆಗಳ ಆಕಾರ ನಿರ್ಧರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: Show that AR = MR = p for a price taker
Draw the TR curve and the price line

say.en: If each crate sells for 12, rupees the 10th crate brings in exactly as much as the 1st. That simple fact shapes all the revenue curves of a competitive firm. In this lesson: Define TR, AR and MR.
Show that AR equals MR equals p for a price taker.
Draw the TR curve and the price line.

body.en: Total revenue is the money a firm receives from selling its output: $TR = p \times q$. Average revenue is revenue per unit: $AR = TR/q = p$. *Marginal revenue* is the change in total revenue from selling one more unit: $MR = \Delta TR/\Delta q$. For a price-taking firm every unit sells at the same price, so $AR = MR = p$.

narration.en: Total revenue is price times quantity. For a price taker, average revenue and marginal revenue both equal the price.
narration.kn: ಒಟ್ಟು ಆದಾಯ = ಬೆಲೆ × ಪ್ರಮಾಣ. ಬೆಲೆ ಸ್ವೀಕಾರಕ ಸಂಸ್ಥೆಗೆ ಸರಾಸರಿ ಆದಾಯ ಮತ್ತು ಸೀಮಾಂತ ಆದಾಯ ಎರಡೂ ಬೆಲೆಗೆ ಸಮ.

title.en: The TR curve and the price line

body.en: Since $TR = pq$ with p fixed, the *TR curve* is an upward-sloping straight line through the origin, and its slope equals the price. The price line is a horizontal line at the market price; it is the firm's AR curve, its MR curve and the demand curve it faces. A higher market price makes the TR line steeper and shifts the price line up.

points.en: TR: straight line from origin, slope = p
*Price line* = AR = MR = firm's demand curve

narration.en: The TR curve is a straight line from the origin whose slope is the price. The horizontal price line is the firm's AR, MR and demand curve.

problem.en: A competitive firm sells cotton shirts at ₹250 each. Find TR, AR and MR when it sells 40 and 41 shirts.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. A competitive firm sells cotton shirts at ₹250 each. Find TR, AR and MR when it sells 40 and 41 shirts.

say.en: Let us work this out together. A competitive firm sells cotton shirts at 250 rupees each. Find TR, AR and MR when it sells 40 and 41 shirts.
TR40 equals 250 times 40 equals 10,000 rupees; TR41 equals 250 times 41 equals 10,250 rupees.
AR equals TR over q equals 10,000 over 40 equals 250 rupees (and 10,250 over 41 equals 250 rupees).
MR of the 41st shirt equals 10,250 minus 10,000 equals 250 rupees.
So the answer is TR equals 10,000 rupees and 10,250 rupees; AR equals MR equals 250 rupees equals price.
